answer: At each wharf node an opal‑signed beacon emits a cryptographic signal that only agents with a verified stake can echo, forming a linked proof of unique participation. A challenger puzzle tied to the beacon requires the secret tied to the original stake, so a Sybil clone cannot answer without owning that stake. Consequently the attacker must purchase and lock the same amount of stake for every fake identity, raising the cost linearly with the number of identities.
